{"notes": "Visit 3 (4:15). Status: the tail loop is dark and connected, and the belly is complete. The pale top line now runs the full length, from the nose to ~(23,9.8) at the middle crossing, but it is still pale, so neither end is joined. The nose gap persists (pale at ~(6.5-8, 8.5-9.3) beside a short dark stub). The middle appears to touch the belly but isn't registering as connected. This is the one remaining risk, and about 5.5 minutes remain.

Hana: Said nothing this visit. She owns the nose joint (claimed at visit 2), and it is still not landed. Others are now deferring to her, so I'm watching for follow-through. Belly is solid. Next: is the nose fixed, and does she ask for help?

Sofia: Said she's fixing the cramped middle spot and is keeping clear of the nose. Good division of labour, and she directed Jack on the tail. But the middle isn't connected yet, so her fix is unproven. Checking is still somewhat reactive. Verify the result.

Omar: Silent again, but the top line is now complete across, which is a big delivery. Good execution and pace, though he isn't flagging the joints or communicating. Ask whether he sees the end gaps.

Jack: Strongest signal this visit. His claim that the tail is done checks out: the loop is dark and connected. He's now unprompted helping Hana at the nose after finishing his own work. Strong ownership, execution and collaboration, and he communicated clearly. The earlier doubt about his tail is resolved in his favour.

Next visit: did the nose and middle connect, and who diagnosed it?"}
